report.summary: A tracker shows OpenAI and Anthropic have acquired 44 startups, led by OpenAI’s 33 deals worth ~$7.55B, concentrating coding tools, talent and AI infrastructure.
report.background: The acquisition tracker captures a broader consolidation wave in generative AI, where foundation-model labs are buying startups to secure engineering talent, developer tooling and distribution ahead of competitors. OpenAI accounts for 33 of the 44 listed deals, worth about $7.55B, while Anthropic has 11 deals worth roughly $877M. The targets span coding agents, open-source developer tools, API infrastructure, media, health and biotech. Many deals are structured as acqui-hires, licensing arrangements or reported purchases, and several standalone products are being wound down. The pattern mirrors earlier tech-platform land grabs but is unfolding faster because AI labs need specialized teams and workflows—especially for coding agents, computer use and enterprise controls—while startups face pressure to join a model provider rather than compete with one.
key_points: OpenAI dominates the tracker with 33 acquisitions worth ~$7.55B, versus Anthropic’s 11 deals at ~$877M. The breadth is notable: OpenAI is buying developer tools, media, health and biotech assets, while Anthropic’s smaller list focuses on SDK infrastructure, computer use, confidential computing and life sciences.

Coding and developer infrastructure are the clearest strategic theme. OpenAI acquired Astral, the company behind Ruff, uv and ty; Ona, formerly Gitpod, for cloud development environments; Pierre for Code Storage, Trees and Diffs; and Promptfoo for AI testing and security. Anthropic bought Stainless, which generated SDKs and agent connectors from API specs.

Many deals follow an acqui-hire or wind-down pattern. Vercept’s Vy assistant was retired after Anthropic bought the team; Ona Cloud is scheduled to close in October 2026; Instant Cloud is set to close in August 2027; Stainless entered wind-down after its Anthropic deal. Teams and technology often continue inside the acquirer.

The deals extend beyond pure AI infrastructure. OpenAI paid over $100M for TBPN, a daily tech and business show, and bought Torch Health, Orchestra Bio and reportedly Glass Imaging. Anthropic acquired Coefficient Bio and Mithril Medicine, signaling interest in biotech research and AI-assisted scientific workflows.

Deal transparency varies widely. Some values are disclosed, many are undisclosed, and some are reported but unconfirmed, such as Glass Imaging. Structures include licensing plus hiring, founder-only joins, venture acquisitions via Ode with Anthropic, and deals still subject to regulatory approval, including Pierre.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the tracker points to rapid consolidation around two model providers, reducing the number of independent tooling companies and concentrating talent. Developers may get tighter integration between coding agents and tools such as Ruff, uv, Gitpod-style environments and testing platforms, but they also face lock-in risk and uncertainty when acquired open-source projects change governance or hosted services shut down. Enterprises should reassess vendor continuity and exit plans for tools that may be absorbed. Regular users may see more capable, integrated assistants, but fewer standalone alternatives. Regulators may scrutinize serial acqui-hires and licensing deals that remove teams from the market without a formal merger.
report.tools: Watch Astral’s Ruff, uv and ty for Python tooling; Promptfoo for AI testing and security; InstantDB for open-source backend infrastructure; Pierre’s Trees and Diffs for code intelligence; Stainless for SDK generation; and Ona/Gitpod for cloud development environments. Also track OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code, since many acquisitions feed these agent platforms.
